caption: The drawing is a simple line illustration done in black ink on an off-white background. It depicts the rear view of a standing bottle shaped like a human figure, draped in what appears to be a long dress or robe. The figure has a headdress or crown-like structure on top of the head and long hair or a head covering flowing down the back. The robe has folds represented by curved lines, and the right-hand side of the garment features embossed text reading “PATENTED FEB 11 1868.” The base of the figure is oval in shape. There are no additional objects or background elements present in the drawing. At the very bottom edge, small printed text reads, “PLATE NUMBER TWO... REAR VIEW OF AMBER INDIAN MAIDEN BITTERS BOTTLE.” with the artist's or draftsman's signature or name.
title: Bitters Bottle (Indian)
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
